description: Drinking water (SDWIS): Search public water systems by state, ZIP code, or county served. Returns system name, PWSID, population served, primary water source, and activity status, in PWSID order; page through a large match with offset and nextOffset. zip_code matches a system's address of record, often an owner's or operator's office far from the area it serves; county (with state) finds the systems serving an area. With has_violation, returns only systems with a current SDWA violation in EPA's ECHO, which applies EPA's Enforcement Response Policy, so it flags fewer systems than SDWIS's unresolved violation records. At least one of state or zip_code is required. Pass a returned pwsid as registry_id to epa_echo_get_facility for the system's drinking-water violations: contaminant, measured level, MCL, status, and enforcement actions.

active_only.description: When true, return only systems SDWIS lists as active (activity code A). The default false also returns inactive systems and ones changed to non-public.

county.description: County the system serves, e.g. "King"; requires state. Case-insensitive, and a trailing "County", "Parish", "Borough", "City and Borough", "Census Area", or "Municipality" is dropped, so "Anchorage" matches Anchorage Municipality. A system matches when one of the counties it serves is this county, so "Harris" does not match Harrison. Punctuation is matched as written ("St. Tammany").

has_violation.description: When true, return only systems with a current SDWA violation in EPA's ECHO, its compliance status for the system, which clears violations SDWIS still lists as unresolved. Works with state, zip_code, county, or a combination.

limit.description: Maximum number of systems to return in one call (1–200, default 50). A larger value, up to 5,000, returns 200 with a notice. Page past it with offset and nextOffset.

offset.description: Number of systems to skip before this page (default 0). Pass the previous call's nextOffset to continue; a value past the end returns an empty page.

pws_type.description: Filter by public water system type: community=permanent residences, non-transient=regular non-residents (schools, businesses), transient=occasional users (campgrounds)

state.description: 2-letter US state or territory code (e.g. "WA", "CA"), or an EPA region code 01–10 for tribal systems, whose primacy agency is the EPA region

zip_code.description: 5-digit ZIP code of the water system's address of record — often its owner's or operator's office, which can be far from the area the system serves. Matches stored ZIP+4s within it; a ZIP+4 searches its 5-digit ZIP. Use county for the systems serving an area.

name: epa_water_search_systems

effectiveQuery.description: The search as the server sent it upstream, in this tool's input names: normalized values, how each text filter matched ("=" exact, "contains", "begins with", "has words"), and defaults that change what comes back. Terms are separated by "; ".

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `no_geographic_filter`: Neither state nor zip_code was provided. `county_requires_state`: county was provided without state. `invalid_state`: state has the 2-character form but is not a US state, DC, territory, freely associated state, UM, NN, or EPA region code. `unmatchable_filter`: county has no letter or digit for EPA's DMAP service to match on. `filter_too_long`: county makes a request longer than EPA's DMAP service accepts. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

guidance.description: Present when more systems may follow: the offset that continues the search.

limitNotice.description: Present when limit was above the cap and the call returned the cap instead.

message.description: Recovery hint when no systems are found. Absent when systems are returned.

nextOffset.description: Offset of the next page: present exactly when more records follow, absent on the last page. Pass it as offset to continue.

notice.description: Present when a check ended before the page filled: a ZIP or county has_violation check read its 1,000-system limit, or the county check reached its read limit with few whole-name matches. nextOffset continues from where it stopped.

systems.description: Matching public water systems, in PWSID order

items.description: Public water system record with PWSID, population served, and violation status

city.description: City of the water system's address of record — often its owner's or operator's office, not necessarily the area it serves

hasViolation.description: True when ECHO reports a current SDWA violation for this system. Present only on has_violation searches, which return only such systems.

isActive.description: Whether this water system is currently active

populationServed.description: Estimated population served by this water system

primarySourceCode.description: Primary water source code (e.g. GW=groundwater, SW=surface water)

pwsid.description: Public Water System ID (PWSID) — unique system identifier

state.description: Primacy agency code: a 2-letter state abbreviation, or the EPA region code 01–10 of a tribal system

type.description: PWS type code: CWS=Community, NTNCWS=Non-transient non-community, TNCWS=Transient non-community

zip.description: ZIP code of the water system's address of record (the value zip_code matches)

totalCount.description: Systems matched before limit and offset. Present when the call saw the whole match: a search from offset 0 with no nextOffset, or a state has_violation search that checked ECHO's whole violator list. Absent otherwise, since EPA's DMAP service reports no match count (follow nextOffset instead).

title: Search Drinking Water Systems
